target_name: Three-Year Knowledge Share with Hard-Book Cheapness
rationale: This is a pure lookback-window tweak (5→3 years) of the archived "Hard-Book Cheapness with Organic Knowledge Share," i.e., a parameter variant with no new economic content, and the R&D-stock depreciation-rate question is itself a well-trodden calibration issue rather than a new mechanism.

Algebraically this is (hard book + R&D stock)/at minus market-cap/at, so it is dominated by the ordinary market-to-assets term — a rescaling of the well-known (intangible-adjusted) book-to-market anomaly rather than a new construct — and the reasoning's claim that the difference is "bounded" is simply false, since market cap per dollar of assets is unbounded above and will dominate the cross-sectional variation.

Internally coherent and correctly signed, but it is a mechanical stacking of two already-archived winners (brand-and-knowledge share, gen-1; innovation runway, gen-7) with the same nested-SUMRANK weighting the archive has used repeatedly, so the likely outcome — modestly higher alpha with a diluted Fama-MacBeth slope — is the already-documented three-leg pattern rather than new information.

Duplicating the knowledge-share leg inside a nested SUMRANK purely to change its implicit weight is a cosmetic re-weighting of two existing parents with no new economic mechanism, and the motivation — recovering fmb without losing alpha — is explicitly curve-fitting to prior evaluation statistics.

The indicator logic is correct (NEG(gdwl/at) > −0.05 does isolate low-goodwill firms) and the joint "no acquired intangibles, meaningful organic R&D" state is a defensible discrete refinement, though it is economically close to the archived "Cheap Builders Versus Cheap Buyers" signal and the binary conditioner will create heavy ties in the second SUMRANK leg.

The gating indicator (R&D stock > hard book) is close to a mechanical restatement of the composite's own knowledge-share leg (share > ~0.5), so multiplying one by the other is largely self-referential rather than an independent regime test, and the construction is otherwise a direct core-swap variant of the archived gen-7 "Cheapness Gated by Accounting Regime."
